3. Application Procedure
3.1 All access applications must be submitted via the Lab Operations Portal (LOP) using the standard request form (Form LOP-ACC-01).
3.2 Applications must be endorsed by the applicant's Principal Investigator (PI) or direct supervisor.
3.3 For Level 2 and Level 3 access, applicants must complete the relevant Biosafety and Chemical Safety modules (see Annex B: Training Matrix) before the application is processed.
3.4 Applications for contractor access must include a valid NRIC/FIN number and a letter of engagement from the hiring PI.

4. Card Issuance and Activation
4.1 Access cards are issued by the Lab Operations Office within five (5) working days of approval.
4.2 Cards are activated for the access level(s) specified in the approved application.
4.3 Temporary cards (valid for up to 14 days) may be issued for short-term visitors, subject to the same endorsement requirements as permanent cards.

5. Access Hours
5.1 Standard access hours are 0700 to 2200, Monday to Saturday.
5.2 After-hours access (2200 to 0700) requires prior approval from the Lab Manager and is only granted for Level 2 and Level 3 personnel who have completed the After-Hours Safety Briefing.
5.3 Public holidays: access is restricted to approved after-hours personnel only.

6. Review and Revocation
6.1 Access privileges are reviewed annually, typically in January.
6.2 Access may be revoked immediately for safety violations, lapsed training certifications, or at the request of the PI.
6.3 Revoked cards must be returned to the Lab Operations Office within three (3) working days.

7. Lost or Stolen Cards
7.1 Lost or stolen cards must be reported to the Lab Operations Office within 24 hours.
7.2 A replacement card will be issued at a cost of S$20.00.
7.3 The lost card will be deactivated immediately upon report.

This draft incorporates the outcomes of the operational review conducted by Lab Operations in September 2025, as well as feedback received during the October consultation window. Sections marked with a change bar indicate substantive revisions. Sections without a change bar are retained from Version 4.0.

**1. Purpose**

1.1 This policy governs physical access to the laboratory premises, including general laboratory areas, specialised equipment rooms, the chemical storage room, and the cold room facility.

1.2 The policy aims to ensure that access is granted only to individuals who have completed the required safety training, that access levels are appropriate to the individual’s role, and that access records are maintained for audit purposes.

**2. Definitions**

2.1 **Cardholder** – Any person issued with a laboratory access card, including research staff, technical staff, postdoctoral fellows (including those on short-term contracts of less than 6 months), graduate students, and visiting researchers.

2.2 **Sponsor** – A Principal Investigator, Laboratory Manager, or designated senior staff member who assumes responsibility for a cardholder’s conduct within the laboratory.

2.3 **Access level** – The combination of doors, rooms, and time windows that a cardholder is permitted to enter.

2.4 **Safety officer** – A staff member designated by the Lab Safety Committee to oversee safety matters during out-of-hours access.

**3. Scope**

3.1 This policy applies to all persons seeking or holding access to the laboratory premises.

3.2 The policy does not apply to areas managed by other departments, such as the building management office or the central equipment depot, which are governed by separate procedures.

**4. Application and Approval Process**

4.1 Applications for new access cards must be submitted through the Lab Access Portal. The application must include the applicant’s name, staff/student ID, department, and the name of the sponsor.

4.2 All applications must be endorsed by the sponsor before processing. Applications without a valid sponsor endorsement will be returned to the applicant.

4.3 The Lab Operations Office will verify the applicant’s employment or enrolment status. For applicants who are not current staff or students, a letter of appointment or visiting researcher agreement must be attached.

4.4 Card activation requires verification of the applicant’s identity. Verification may be conducted in person at the Lab Operations Office or via video call for off-site researchers. For video-call verification, the applicant must show their NRIC, passport, or other government-issued photo identification. The verification session will be recorded and the recording retained for 90 days.

4.5 New cardholders must complete the online laboratory safety induction before the card is activated. The induction certificate must be uploaded to the portal.

4.6 Access cards are issued for a maximum period of one year. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 14 days before the expiry date.

**5. Access Hours and Zones**

5.1 Standard access hours are Monday to Friday, 0700 to 1900, for general laboratory areas.

5.2 Access outside standard hours is permitted for cardholders who have completed the out-of-hours safety briefing. This briefing is valid for one year and must be renewed annually.

5.3 Access to the chemical storage room is limited to weekdays, 0900 to 1700, and Saturday, 0900 to 1300, subject to the presence of a designated safety officer. The safety officer roster will be published every Friday for the following week.

**6. Lost, Stolen, or Damaged Cards**

6.1 Cardholders must report a lost or stolen access card to the Lab Operations Office within 24 hours of becoming aware of the loss. Reports may be made by email to labaccess@nus.edu.sg or by phone at 6516-XXXX during office hours.

6.2 Upon receipt of a loss report, the card will be deactivated immediately. A replacement card will be issued upon payment of the prevailing replacement fee, currently $50.00 (inclusive of GST).

6.3 If a card is found after a replacement has been issued, the original card must be returned to the Lab Operations Office. The returned card will be destroyed. No refund will be given for the replacement fee.

6.4 Cardholders who damage their cards through normal wear and tear may request a free replacement. Damage caused by misuse, such as immersion in liquid, bending, or exposure to extreme heat, will be treated as a lost card and the replacement fee will apply.

6.5 Temporary access cards are available for visitors and short-term collaborators. These cards are valid for a maximum of 14 consecutive days and must be returned to the Lab Operations Office on or before the expiry date. A late return penalty of $10.00 per day will be applied to the sponsoring department.

**7. Cardholder Responsibilities**

7.1 Access cards are issued to individuals and must not be shared, lent, or transferred to any other person. Cardholders are responsible for all activities conducted under their card.

7.2 Cardholders must not attempt to gain access to areas for which they do not hold the appropriate authorisation. This includes tailgating, which is the act of following an authorised person into a restricted area without presenting a valid card.

7.3 Cardholders must display their access card visibly while in the laboratory. The card lanyard must be worn around the neck or clipped to the upper body clothing.

7.4 Any change in the cardholder’s employment or student status must be reported to the Lab Operations Office within 7 days. The card will be deactivated upon the termination of the cardholder’s affiliation with the University.

7.5 Cardholders who are issued a card under a visiting researcher agreement must return the card to the Lab Operations Office on the last day of their visit. The card must be surrendered in person or by registered post.

**8. Suspension and Revocation of Access**

8.1 The Lab Operations Office may suspend a card immediately if there is reasonable cause to believe that the card has been compromised, or that the cardholder has violated any provision of this policy.

8.2 A suspension will be communicated to the cardholder and the sponsor by email. The cardholder may appeal the suspension in writing to the Lab Safety Committee within 14 days of the date of the suspension notice.

8.3 Access privileges may be revoked permanently for repeated violations of this policy, for unauthorised disclosure of laboratory access codes, or for any action that compromises the safety or security of the laboratory.

8.4 Revocation of access does not preclude the University from taking further disciplinary action under applicable staff or student conduct regulations.

**9. Out-of-Hours Access Protocol**

9.1 Out-of-hours access is defined as access between 1900 and 0700 on weekdays, and at any time on weekends or public holidays.

9.2 To be eligible for out-of-hours access, a cardholder must have completed the out-of-hours safety briefing within the past 12 months. The briefing is conducted online and takes approximately 30 minutes. Upon completion, the cardholder's access rights will be updated within 2 working days.

3. Application Procedure
3.1 All access applications must be submitted via the Lab Operations Portal (LOP) using the standard request form (Form LOP-ACC-01).
3.2 Applications must be endorsed by the applicant's Principal Investigator (PI) or direct supervisor.
3.3 For Level 2 and Level 3 access, applicants must complete the relevant Biosafety and Chemical Safety modules (see Annex B: Training Matrix) before the application is processed.
3.4 Applications for contractor access must include a valid NRIC/FIN number and a letter of engagement from the hiring PI.

4. Card Issuance and Activation
4.1 Access cards are issued by the Lab Operations Office within five (5) working days of approval.
4.2 Cards are activated for the access level(s) specified in the approved application.
4.3 Temporary cards (valid for up to 14 days) may be issued for short-term visitors, subject to the same endorsement requirements as permanent cards.

5. Access Hours
5.1 Standard access hours are 0700 to 2200, Monday to Saturday.
5.2 After-hours access (2200 to 0700) requires prior approval from the Lab Manager and is only granted for Level 2 and Level 3 personnel who have completed the After-Hours Safety Briefing.
5.3 Public holidays: access is restricted to approved after-hours personnel only.

6. Review and Revocation
6.1 Access privileges are reviewed annually, typically in January.
6.2 Access may be revoked immediately for safety violations, lapsed training certifications, or at the request of the PI.
6.3 Revoked cards must be returned to the Lab Operations Office within three (3) working days.

7. Lost or Stolen Cards
7.1 Lost or stolen cards must be reported to the Lab Operations Office within 24 hours.
7.2 A replacement card will be issued at a cost of S$20.00.
7.3 The lost card will be deactivated immediately upon report.

**Annex A: Lab Access Policy – Draft Versions**

**Version 5.0 (Draft) – for consultation**

Status: Draft for consultation. To be tabled at the LSC meeting on 20/11/2025.
Approval date: Pending
Supersedes: Version 4.0 upon approval

This draft incorporates the outcomes of the operational review conducted by Lab Operations in September 2025, as well as feedback received during the October consultation window. Sections marked with a change bar indicate substantive revisions. Sections without a change bar are retained from Version 4.0.

**1. Purpose**

1.1 This policy governs physical access to the laboratory premises, including general laboratory areas, specialised equipment rooms, the chemical storage room, and the cold room facility.

1.2 The policy aims to ensure that access is granted only to individuals who have completed the required safety training, that access levels are appropriate to the individual’s role, and that access records are maintained for audit purposes.

**2. Definitions**

2.1 **Cardholder** – Any person issued with a laboratory access card, including research staff, technical staff, postdoctoral fellows (including those on short-term contracts of less than 6 months), graduate students, and visiting researchers.

2.2 **Sponsor** – A Principal Investigator, Laboratory Manager, or designated senior staff member who assumes responsibility for a cardholder’s conduct within the laboratory.

2.3 **Access level** – The combination of doors, rooms, and time windows that a cardholder is permitted to enter.

2.4 **Safety officer** – A staff member designated by the Lab Safety Committee to oversee safety matters during out-of-hours access.

**3. Scope**

3.1 This policy applies to all persons seeking or holding access to the laboratory premises.

3.2 The policy does not apply to areas managed by other departments, such as the building management office or the central equipment depot, which are governed by separate procedures.

**4. Application and Approval Process**

4.1 Applications for new access cards must be submitted through the Lab Access Portal. The application must include the applicant’s name, staff/student ID, department, and the name of the sponsor.

4.2 All applications must be endorsed by the sponsor before processing. Applications without a valid sponsor endorsement will be returned to the applicant.

4.3 The Lab Operations Office will verify the applicant’s employment or enrolment status. For applicants who are not current staff or students, a letter of appointment or visiting researcher agreement must be attached.

4.4 Card activation requires verification of the applicant’s identity. Verification may be conducted in person at the Lab Operations Office or via video call for off-site researchers. For video-call verification, the applicant must show their NRIC, passport, or other government-issued photo identification. The verification session will be recorded and the recording retained for 90 days.

4.5 New cardholders must complete the online laboratory safety induction before the card is activated. The induction certificate must be uploaded to the portal.

4.6 Access cards are issued for a maximum period of one year. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 14 days before the expiry date.

**5. Access Hours and Zones**

5.1 Standard access hours are Monday to Friday, 0700 to 1900, for general laboratory areas.

5.2 Access outside standard hours is permitted for cardholders who have completed the out-of-hours safety briefing. This briefing is valid for one year and must be renewed annually.

5.3 Access to the chemical storage room is limited to weekdays, 0900 to 1700, and Saturday, 0900 to 1300, subject to the presence of a designated safety officer. The safety officer roster will be published every Friday for the following week.

**Draft v0.9 (Working Copy) – 14/03/2025**

**6. Lost, Stolen, or Damaged Cards**

6.1 Cardholders must report a lost or stolen access card to the Lab Operations Office within 24 hours of becoming aware of the loss. Reports may be made by email to labaccess@nus.edu.sg or by phone at 6516-XXXX during office hours.

6.2 Upon receipt of a loss report, the card will be deactivated immediately. A replacement card will be issued upon payment of the prevailing replacement fee, currently $50.00 (inclusive of GST).

6.3 If a card is found after a replacement has been issued, the original card must be returned to the Lab Operations Office. The returned card will be destroyed. No refund will be given for the replacement fee.

6.4 Cardholders who damage their cards through normal wear and tear may request a free replacement. Damage caused by misuse, such as immersion in liquid, bending, or exposure to extreme heat, will be treated as a lost card and the replacement fee will apply.

6.5 Temporary access cards are available for visitors and short-term collaborators. These cards are valid for a maximum of 14 consecutive days and must be returned to the Lab Operations Office on or before the expiry date. A late return penalty of $10.00 per day will be applied to the sponsoring department.

**7. Cardholder Responsibilities**

7.1 Access cards are issued to individuals and must not be shared, lent, or transferred to any other person. Cardholders are responsible for all activities conducted under their card.

7.2 Cardholders must not attempt to gain access to areas for which they do not hold the appropriate authorisation. This includes tailgating, which is the act of following an authorised person into a restricted area without presenting a valid card.

7.3 Cardholders must display their access card visibly while in the laboratory. The card lanyard must be worn around the neck or clipped to the upper body clothing.

7.4 Any change in the cardholder’s employment or student status must be reported to the Lab Operations Office within 7 days. The card will be deactivated upon the termination of the cardholder’s affiliation with the University.

7.5 Cardholders who are issued a card under a visiting researcher agreement must return the card to the Lab Operations Office on the last day of their visit. The card must be surrendered in person or by registered post.

**8. Suspension and Revocation of Access**

8.1 The Lab Operations Office may suspend a card immediately if there is reasonable cause to believe that the card has been compromised, or that the cardholder has violated any provision of this policy.

8.2 A suspension will be communicated to the cardholder and the sponsor by email. The cardholder may appeal the suspension in writing to the Lab Safety Committee within 14 days of the date of the suspension notice.

8.3 Access privileges may be revoked permanently for repeated violations of this policy, for unauthorised disclosure of laboratory access codes, or for any action that compromises the safety or security of the laboratory.

8.4 Revocation of access does not preclude the University from taking further disciplinary action under applicable staff or student conduct regulations.

---

**Draft v1.0 (Proposed Final) – 22/03/2025**

**9. Out-of-Hours Access Protocol**

9.1 Out-of-hours access is defined as access between 1900 and 0700 on weekdays, and at any time on weekends or public holidays.

9.2 To be eligible for out-of-hours access, a cardholder must have completed the out-of-hours safety briefing within the past 12 months. The briefing is conducted online and takes approximately 30 minutes. Upon completion, the cardholder's access rights will be updated within 2 working days.

**3.1 Minor Incident – Lab 3-2 (Centrifuge Tube Leak)**

Dr. M. Hadi reported a minor incident that occurred on 24/02/2026 in Lab 3-2. A researcher from the Tissue Engineering Group was centrifuging a sample containing a non-infectious reagent. The tube failed during operation, causing a minor leak within the centrifuge bucket. The researcher followed the spill response protocol, decontaminated the area, and submitted an incident report to the Safety Officer. No injuries were reported. The centrifuge has been inspected by the manufacturer's service team and is back in service.

The Chair reminded members that centrifuge tube integrity checks should be part of routine laboratory housekeeping. Dr. L. Fernandez noted that her group will review their centrifuge tube usage and ensure that tubes are not reused beyond the manufacturer's recommended cycles.

Mr. J. Lim reported a near miss observed during a routine weekly inspection on 26/02/2026. A trolley containing cardboard boxes was found temporarily blocking the emergency exit in Lab 4-3. **Minutes of Previous Meeting (17/02/2026)**

The minutes of the previous meeting were circulated by email on 20/02/2026. Members confirmed the minutes as a true record. No amendments were proposed.

**Matters Arising**

1.  **Automated Liquid Handling Systems:** The Safety Officer reported that a preliminary count of automated liquid handling systems across the laboratories has been completed. The count currently stands at 14 systems in active use. The Chair noted that this is below the threshold that would trigger a review of occupancy limits, but the Safety Officer will continue to monitor the number and report back at the next meeting.
2.  **Fume Hood in Lab 4-1:** The new fume hood installation in Lab 4-1 has been completed and commissioned. The Safety Officer confirmed that the hood has passed all performance tests and is now in service. The occupancy limit for Lab 4-1 remains unchanged at 6 persons, as the new hood does not affect the overall safe occupancy of the laboratory.

**Agenda Item 1: Report on Recent Safety Incidents**

The Safety Officer reported on the following incidents that occurred during the month of February 2026:

1.  **Incident Report No. 2026-021:** On 18/02/2026 at approximately 15:30, a minor chemical spill (approx. 50 ml of 1M hydrochloric acid) occurred in Lab 3-2. The spill was contained immediately by the researcher involved, who was wearing appropriate PPE. The spill was cleaned up using the spill kit located in the lab, and the area was cordoned off until the cleanup was verified by the Safety Coordinator. No injuries were reported. An incident report has been filed, and the researcher has been reminded to ensure that all containers are properly sealed when not in use.
2.  **Incident Report No. 2026-022:** On 25/02/2026, a staff member in Lab 2-1 reported a minor cut sustained while handling broken glassware. The cut was treated at the first aid station, and the staff member was advised to seek further medical attention if necessary. The incident was attributed to improper disposal of broken glassware. The Safety Officer will be conducting a refresher training session on proper glassware handling and disposal procedures.
3.  **Near Miss Report:** On 02/03/2026, a near miss was reported in Lab 4-2 involving an electrical cord that was frayed and exposed. The cord was discovered by a researcher who immediately reported it to the Safety Coordinator. The equipment was taken out of service, and the cord was replaced. The Safety Officer reminded members to conduct regular visual inspections of all electrical equipment in their laboratories.

**Action Items:**
- Safety Officer to circulate a reminder to all laboratory users regarding proper glassware disposal procedures. (Due: 24/03/2026)
- Safety Coordinator to include a check of electrical cords in the monthly laboratory inspection checklist. (Due: 31/03/2026)

Dr. S. Wong reported that the Laser Safety Training session scheduled for 16/03/2026 (Monday) has been conducted. A total of 12 researchers attended the session.
